_publishAt_is_null_on_purpose: publish-all.mjs REFUSES to run while youtube.publishAt or facebook.publishAt is
null, and that is the safety property wanted here: the packaging is authored and
reviewable, but nothing can be scheduled until a human sets the dates. A plausible
placeholder date would pass validation and schedule the wrong slot, and a published
film cannot be quietly corrected — the subscriber notification has already gone out.
DrJ sets these. Nothing about this file constitutes approval to publish.
_syntheticContent: TRUE, and it must stay true. Six Higgsfield-generated stills are used as the
backplates behind the data frames (grounds.json). They are abstract and textless,
but they are generated imagery, so the YouTube 'Altered content' disclosure applies
and the description says so in words. publish-all.mjs cross-checks this against the
AI-generated stamp in out/footage/LICENSES.md in both directions and refuses on a
mismatch. If the grounds are ever dropped in favour of flat near-black, this flag
and the description line come out together.

youtube.title: I'm a Doctor. Here's What That Xylitol Study Actually Says.
youtube.description:
A study presented at ESC Congress 2026 in Munich followed 17,710 people and
found higher blood levels of xylitol tracked with more heart attacks, strokes
and deaths. That part is real, and it fits a pattern going back to erythritol
in 2023.

But there's a detail in the study design that almost none of the coverage
mentioned, and it changes what the finding means. I go through the numbers,
the mechanism, the published counter-arguments from other cardiologists, the
dose in an actual packet of gum — and the labelling gap that means you can't
measure your own exposure even if you want to.

This is my professional read of published research. It is not medical advice
for any individual. Observational studies show association, not causation.
Talk to your own doctor about your own situation.

Some abstract background textures in this video were generated with AI. Every
figure, chart and number on screen is rendered from the sourced data below.

CHAPTERS
00:00  I've been giving this advice for years
00:38  What they found in Munich
02:05  Why this study is harder to dismiss
03:05  Five cohorts, two sweeteners, one direction
04:20  Clotting, not cholesterol
05:20  The 13 minutes nobody reported
06:55  The argument back — and a disclosure
08:10  Your packet, and the gap on the label
09:35  The part that isn't debated
10:10  How I actually read it

SOURCES
ESC press release, 26 Aug 2026: https://www.escardio.org/news/press/press-releases/xylitol-may-increase-the-risk-of-cardiovascular-events/
Witkowski et al., Eur Heart J 2024;45:2439-2452: https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae244
Witkowski/Hazen et al., Nature Medicine 2023;29:710-718: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-023-02223-9
Wölnerhanssen et al., EHJ commentary: https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae730
Bonomini et al., EHJ commentary: https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehae731
NIH Research Matters, erythritol: https://www.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/erythritol-cardiovascular-events
Merck Veterinary Manual, xylitol toxicosis in dogs: https://www.merckvetmanual.com/toxicology/food-hazards/xylitol-toxicosis-in-dogs
